title: The Gift of Words — Writing to Glorify God
description: Test your understanding of creative writing concepts from a Biblical perspective. This quiz covers the power of words, descriptive writing, short story basics, poetry, journaling, and writing as worship.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 18:21, what power do words carry?
options: Words have no real impact on others
Words have the power of life and death
Words are only powerful when spoken aloud
Words only matter in formal writing
questions.explanation: Proverbs 18:21 teaches that 'the tongue has the power of life and death.' Our words — spoken and written — can build up or tear down, encourage or discourage.

questions.question: What does the writing principle 'show, don't tell' mean?
options: Always include illustrations with your writing
Use vivid sensory details to let the reader experience the scene rather than just stating facts
Tell the reader exactly how to feel about the story
Show your writing to as many people as possible
questions.explanation: 'Show, don't tell' means using specific, sensory details to create a vivid experience for the reader, rather than simply stating emotions or facts.

questions.question: What are the three basic building blocks of a short story?
options: Introduction, body, conclusion
Character, setting, and plot
Title, author, and publisher
Nouns, verbs, and adjectives
questions.explanation: Every short story is built on three essential elements: character (who the story is about), setting (where and when it takes place), and plot (what happens).

questions.question: Why is conflict important in a story?
options: It makes the story violent and exciting
It is not important — good stories should be peaceful
It gives the character a problem to face and drives the story forward
It is only needed in long novels, not short stories
questions.explanation: Conflict — a problem or challenge the character must face — is the engine of a story. Without conflict, there is no reason for the reader to keep reading. The character's response to conflict reveals their growth.

questions.question: What is parallelism in Hebrew poetry, as found in the Psalms?
options: Two lines that rhyme perfectly
Two lines that express a similar idea in different words
Writing in two columns on the page
Repeating the same word at the beginning of every line
questions.explanation: Parallelism is a key feature of Hebrew poetry where two lines express a similar idea using different words. For example, Psalm 19:1: 'The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands.'

questions.question: What is one of the main benefits of keeping a journal as a Christian?
options: It helps you get better grades in school
It records your spiritual journey and helps you remember God's faithfulness
It is required by most churches
It replaces the need to read the Bible
questions.explanation: Journaling helps you record and reflect on your spiritual journey — your prayers, God's answers, lessons learned from Scripture, and how God is working in your life. It helps you remember His faithfulness over time.

questions.question: According to Colossians 3:17, how should Christians approach their creative writing?
options: Writing should only be done on Sundays
Christians should avoid creative writing entirely
Whatever we do, including writing, should be done in the name of the Lord Jesus
Writing is acceptable only if it directly quotes the Bible
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:17 teaches that whatever we do — in word or deed — should be done in the name of the Lord Jesus. This means our creative writing can be an act of worship when done with gratitude and a desire to honor God.

questions.question: What is a simile?
options: A statement that one thing IS another thing
A comparison of two unlike things using 'like' or 'as'
A type of poem with exactly fourteen lines
A word that sounds like what it describes
questions.explanation: A simile compares two unlike things using the words 'like' or 'as.' For example, 'The lake was smooth as glass.' Similes help readers see familiar things in new and vivid ways.
